game_identity.player_fantasy: Be the last maintenance runner carrying unstable charge from a central core to failing relays fast enough to keep the network alive.
game_identity.central_interaction: Route, recharge, carry, and transfer charge between a central core and four decaying relay beacons.

playable_loop: Move -> recharge at core -> choose upper/lower passage -> carry charge -> read changing relay urgency -> choose which relay to service -> touch beacon to transfer -> manage decay -> stabilize all four or black out -> retry

controls.move: WASD, arrow keys, or standard-mapped gamepad left stick / D-pad
controls.restart: R, Restart button, or standard-mapped gamepad Start

technology_stack: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript Canvas; local/offline browser; no dependencies
current_milestone: Adaptive Completion Slice: determine whether the accepted player-visible maintenance state can drive a complete run from the normal reset state without a prewritten relay-service sequence. Systems/QA should declare one reasonable state-driven decision/recharge/service policy before execution, recompute each next action from current accepted state, and continue to WON, BLACKOUT, or a fixed generous budget that demonstrates a repeatable non-terminal cycle/stall. The policy may use runner charge, relay energies/online state, current position/route geometry, fixed thresholds, and deterministic tie-breaks, but must not encode a future relay order, branch-specific script, or future-state lookahead to force success. Record target history, core returns, elapsed time, runner charge, relay energies/online count, route/service/recharge costs where practical, and terminal margin/outcome or cycle evidence. Success and failure are both valid findings; do not tune mid-run. Test the accepted model before adding hazards, relay classes, scoring, another chamber, resources, or a new primary verb. Human/fresh-player PLAYTESTED evidence remains required before claims that people can infer the strategy or find it understandable, fair, tense, balanced, or fun.

evidence_status.run_consequence_slice: COMPLETED on accepted main through Systems PR #45, merged as test-only evidence on the unchanged runtime. Both branches begin from the accepted ~13.30s R1-versus-R3 decision and then use one identical policy: return to core, fully recharge, select the lowest-energy relay, break energy ties by shortest measured route then relay index, and service for exactly 1.00s. Cheap-first follows R1 > R3 > R4 > R2 > R3 > R4 > R2; urgent-first follows R3 > R4 > R2 > R1 > R3 > R4 > R2. After three follow-ups they still choose different fourth total targets and differ by more than 20 recovery-burden energy. By the sixth follow-up the live state substantially reconverges: both have runner charge about 45.312, relay energies 0.000 / 40.240 / 0.000 / 18.358, recovery burden 86.642, the same online count/final target, and nearly the same position, while urgent-first remains about 1.04s later with about 0.92s more cumulative travel. Neither branch reaches WON or BLACKOUT inside the bounded horizon. Director interpretation: recoverable consequence is coherent; reconvergence alone is not a defect or justification for manufactured complexity.
evidence_status.adaptive_completion_slice: OPEN / NOT YET CHARACTERIZED. Accepted main proves a full WON path through a fixed scripted relay-service regression and separately proves state-driven mid-run route/urgency decisions, decision chains, and recoverable run consequence. It does not yet prove that a declared state-driven policy using only current accepted player-visible/mechanically explicit state can carry a fresh normal run to WON, BLACKOUT, or a bounded repeatable cycle without a prewritten target order or future-state lookahead.
